name: Peter Paul Rubens
findings: Uses smoky black 1.4x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 763 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, oxblood turns up as a small accent in 80% of the paintings that hold it, 1.9x the archive's rate (from 763 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, greyish black turns up as the lightest note in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 5.4x the archive's rate (from 763 paintings here).
Pairs fallen leaf with honey yellow more than chance would predict (4 of 763 paintings here).
Pairs dim grey with nickel more than chance would predict (3 of 763 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark olive brown, bistre) covers 54% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark olive brown to smoky black, black.
Paints most like Angelica Kauffmann among the painters in this archive, by palette.
